notes:
Summary: Cadence Edge runs perception and planning pipelines that call an LLM-backed route scoring service for fast candidate ranking and context-aware map retrieval. Primary interest: Redwood Dedicated with on-prem control plane. Key asks: firm throughput guarantees (packets/sec -> inference QPS mapping), 99.9/99.99 latency SLOs for <30ms token latency in critical path, reserved GPU planning for peak driving windows, plus contractual SLA language for mitigations and penalty tiers.

Workload specifics and model tuning requests (from SE sessions):
- Models under consideration: LlamaX-70B (float16 baseline), open-llm-13B distilled variant for lower-latency endpoints. Want Redwood to validate quantization profiles (4/8-bit symmetric and asymmetric) against perception-context prompts.
- Context length: typical route+map history ~8k tokens, occasional full diagnostic dumps to 32k; need dynamic context truncation and KV cache management. Testing plan: simulate 90% warm-starts (KV hits) and 10% cold-starts.
- Batching/KV cache: aggressive micro-batching for background scoring, but must support single-request low-latency path for safety-critical calls. Request Redwood recommended batching windows (5–15ms) and fallback to single-token-mode for <5ms tails.
- Quantization/Perf tradeoffs: require Redwood to run head-to-head with and without quantization to produce regression matrix: P50/P95/P99 latency, output-quality delta (ROUGE/embedding-sim), and memory footprint.
- Reserved GPUs: initial ask = capacity for sustained 6k qps (small model endpoints) + burst 25k qps for map-rebuild jobs; propose hybrid pool (dedicated + burst on shared). Need HW sizing (H100 equiv or L4c) and pod counts per model profile.
- SLOs & SLA negotiation points: define SLOs per route (critical vs background), outline maintenance windows, fall-back model routing, and financial credits for missed SLO tiers. Legal requested sample SLA appendix.

Operational/Integration notes:
- Security: must integrate with internal SSO (SAML), KMS for model keys, audit logs to central ELK, and data residency constraints for map tiles. On-prem Private deployment preferred for low-latency region; Redwood console must expose token-level cost for each endpoint.
- Testing artifacts: Fireflies id: fireflies_55829 (POC kickoff), Gmail thread: thread/gmail/CA-POC-8241, Drive: drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_cadence/poc-redwood-pricing-deck (pricing + test plan), Jira: INF-3421 (POC infra), INF-3498 (tail-latency investigation).

Stakeholder quotes / shorthand from meetings:
- "Can you guarantee 30ms P99 for the critical scoring path?" — Head of Perception.
- "We will not accept >1% regression in candidate ranking accuracy with quantization." — Lead ML Engineer.

Next steps (detailed):
1) Redwood to deliver reserved GPU SOW with model-specific pod counts and cost delta for quantization profiles (due 2026-03-05).
2) Legal to receive draft SLA appendix and escalation flow (AE owns follow-up).
3) SE to run A/B quality tests on 70B float16 vs 8-bit quant on provided dev dataset (timeline: 2 weeks).
4) Cadence to provision on-prem test rack for 2-week soak test (ops team scheduling).

Misc: cost-sensitivity high for burst capacity; prefer predictable committed spend with clear overage pricing. POC success metric: meet 99.9 P95 token latency and <0.5% ranking delta vs baseline.
sla_requirements: P95 < 20ms (critical), P99 < 30ms (critical), P99 (background) < 100ms; uptime 99.95% monthly; credit tiers defined per missed SLO
